propositions: An errored side in a parity pair carries a synthetic decision ('dropped') that was never produced by the model, causing it to be counted as a decision flip when differing from the other arm's real verdict.

The decision_flips comprehension at parity.py:107 compares decision fields without an errored guard, conflating non-verdicts with model verdicts and violating the documented contract that errored is 'not a model verdict'.
A single transient infrastructure error (e.g. ThrottlingException) fails the parity gating slot as a spurious model-quality regression because criterion (b) treats any flip as never acceptable.
The parity report cannot distinguish fabricated flips caused by errors from genuine model-quality regressions, because metrics lack per-pair detail and errored_pairs was not surfaced.
Errored pairs must be excluded from decision_flips and counted into a separate errored_pairs metric, with the guard keyed on the errored flag rather than decision-vocabulary membership.
